transcript.en: Right, well, for our presentation shall I start with the early life of Thor Heyerdahl?
transcript.zh: 我们的演讲能不能以Thor Heyerdahl的早期生活为开头？

transcript.en: Sure.
transcript.zh: 没问题。

transcript.en: Why don't you begin with describing the type of boy he was, especially his passion for collecting things.
transcript.zh: 你在演讲开始的时候可以描述一下他在孩子时期的性格，尤其是他对于收集东西的热情。

transcript.en: That's right, he had his own little museum.
transcript.zh: 没错，他还有个自己的小小博物馆呢。

transcript.en: And I think it's unusual for children to develop their own values and not join in their parents' hobbies; I'm thinking of how Heyerdahl wouldn't go hunting with his dad, for example.
transcript.zh: 而且我觉得在童年时期就能发展出自己的价值观而不是一味模仿父母的兴趣爱好，实在是太不寻常了。比如Heyerdahl不愿意和他爸爸一起去打猎。

transcript.en: Yeah, he preferred to learn about nature by listening to his mother read to him.
transcript.zh: 是的，他更愿意通过他妈妈念书给他听的这种方式来了解大自然。

transcript.en: And quite early on he knew he wanted to become an explorer when he grew up.
transcript.zh: 而且他很早就知道自己长大之后想要成为一名探险家。

transcript.en: That came from his camping trips he went on in Norway I think ...
transcript.zh: 我想这个想法是在他去挪威参加露营旅行的时候产生的......

transcript.en: No, it was climbing that he spent his time on as a young man.
transcript.zh: 不，是在他年轻的时候花了很多时间爬山时产生的。

transcript.en: Oh, right ...
After university he married a classmate and together, they decided to experience living on a small island, to find out how harsh weather conditions shaped people's lifestyles.
transcript.zh: 大学毕业之后，他和同班的一个女生结了婚，然后他们俩共同决定体验一下居住在小岛上的感受，去弄清楚严酷的天气条件对人们的生活方式会有哪些影响。

transcript.en: As part of their preparation before they left home, they learnt basic survival skills like building a shelter.
transcript.zh: 他们离开家之前，做的准备工作的一部分就是学习一些基本的生存技能，比如建造一个住所。

transcript.en: I guess they needed that knowledge in order to live wild in a remote location with few inhabitants, cut off by the sea, which is what they were aiming to do.
transcript.zh: 我想他们要在一个人迹罕至的荒岛上生存，被大海分隔开，这种知识是必需的，而生活在那种地方也正是他们的目的所在。

transcript.en: An important part of your talk should be the radical theory Heyerdahl formed from examining mysterious ancient carvings that he happened to find on the island.
transcript.zh: 你的演讲中应该包括的一个重要部分，就是Heyerdahl通过研究他无意中在荒岛上发现的神秘的古代石雕而形成的激进理论。

transcript.en: I think you should finish with that.
transcript.zh: 我觉得你应该把这部分内容完成。

transcript.en: OK.
transcript.zh: 好的。

transcript.en: All right, Victor, so after your part I'll talk about Thor Heyerdahl's adult life, continuing from the theory he had about Polynesian migration.
transcript.zh: 好的，Victor，你演讲完之后，我就从Thor Heyerdahl关于波利尼西亚移民的理论继续，讲一讲他的成年人生活。

transcript.en: Up until that time of course, academics had believed that humans first migrated to the islands in Polynesia from Asia, in the west.
transcript.zh: 在他之前，学术界一直认为最初移民到波利尼西亚岛上的人类是从西边，亚洲过来的。

transcript.en: Yes, they thought that travel from the east was impossible, because of the huge, empty stretch of ocean that lies between the islands and the nearest inhabited land.
transcript.zh: 是的，他们认为从东边过来是不可能的，因为在海岛和最近的有人居住的土地之间隔着一段巨大而空阔的海洋。

transcript.en: Yes, but Heyerdahl spent ages studying the cloud movements, ocean currents and wind patterns to find if it was actually possible.
transcript.zh: 没错，不过Heyerdahl花了好多年的时间研究云层运动、洋流和风的模式来探究这种理论究竟可不可行。

transcript.en: And another argument was that there was no tradition of large ship building in the communities lying to the east of Polynesia.
transcript.zh: 另外一个争议就是，当时的学术界认为生活在波利尼西亚东部的部落没有大规模造船的惯例。

transcript.en: But Heyerdahl knew they made lots of coastal voyages in locally built canoes.
transcript.zh: 但是Heyerdahl知道那些部落的人使用当地建造的独木舟进行过很多次沿海航行。

transcript.en: Yes, or sailing on rafts, as was shown by the long voyage that Heyerdahl did next.
transcript.zh: 对，或者用木筏航行，就像Heyerdahl接下来做的一次远途航行展示的那样。

transcript.en: It was an incredibly risky journey to undertake sometimes I wonder if he did that trip for private reasons, you know?
transcript.zh: 进行那样的一段旅程是极其危险的，有时候我都好奇他那么做是不是为了一些私人原因。

transcript.en: To show others that he could have spectacular adventures.
transcript.zh: 比如向别人展示他可以进行一些惊人的冒险。

transcript.en: What do you think, Olivia?
transcript.zh: 你觉得呢，Olivia？

transcript.en: Well, I think it was more a matter of simply trying out his idea, to see if migration from the east was possible.
transcript.zh: 我觉得这也许只是他想要试试自己的想法而已，看看从东边迁移过来有没有可能性。

transcript.en: Yes, that's probably it.
transcript.zh: 嗯，可能就是这样吧。

transcript.en: And the poor guy suffered a bit at that time because the war forced him to stop his work for some years ...
transcript.zh: 嗯，可能就是这样吧。这个可怜的家伙当时受了不少苦，因为战争使得他不得不停止研究，而这一停就是好几年。

transcript.en: Yes. When he got started again and planned his epic voyage, do you think it was important to him that he achieve it before anyone else did?
transcript.zh: 是的。之后他又重新开始研究并且策划了他的那次伟大旅程，你觉得他在别人做到之前抢先完成了这件事对他来说重不重要？

transcript.en: Um, I haven't read anywhere that that was his motivation.
transcript.zh: 嗯......我还没在任何地方读到过把这一点当做他的动力的。

transcript.en: The most important factor seems to have been that he use only ancient techniques and local materials to build his raft.
transcript.zh: 最重要的因素似乎是他只用了古代的技术和当地的材料来建造他的木筏。

transcript.en: Yes.
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.en: I wonder how fast it went.
transcript.zh: 我很好奇那艘木筏速度能有多快。

transcript.en: Well, it took them 97 days from South America to the Pacific Islands.
transcript.zh: 他们从南美洲航行到太平洋岛屿花了97天。

transcript.en: Mm.
transcript.zh: 嗯…

transcript.en: And after that, Heyerdahl went to Easter Island, didn't he?
transcript.zh: 在那之后，Heyerdahl又去了复活节岛，对吗？

transcript.en: We should mention the purpose of that trip.
transcript.zh: 我们应该提一下他那趟旅程的目的。

transcript.en: I think he sailed there in a boat made out of reeds.
transcript.zh: 我记得他是划着一艘用芦苇做成的船到那儿的。

transcript.en: No, that was later on in Egypt, Olivia.
transcript.zh: 不是，Olivia，他后来去埃及的时候才是划着芦苇做的船。

transcript.en: Oh, yes, that's right.
transcript.zh: 哦，对对对。

transcript.en: But what he wanted to do was talk to the local people about their old stone carvings and then make one himself to learn more about the process.
transcript.zh: 不过他想要做的只是跟当地人聊一聊他们古老的石雕，然后自己做一个出来，以便对这个过程更加了解。

transcript.en: I see.
transcript.zh: 我知道了。

transcript.en: Well, what a great life.
transcript.zh: 他的人生真是太伟大了。

transcript.en: Even though many of his theories have been disproven, he certainly left a lasting impression on many disciplines, didn't he?
transcript.zh: 即使他的很多理论都被驳倒了，但是他无疑在很多学科上都留下了深远的影响，不是吗？

transcript.en: To my mind, he was the first person to establish what modern academics call practical archaeology.
transcript.zh: 在我心中，他是第一个建立现代学术界称为实用考古学的人。

transcript.en: I mean, that they try to recreate something from the past today, like he did with his raft trip.
transcript.zh: 如今学者们都试图重现过去的事物，就像他进行木筏航行的做法一样。

transcript.en: It's unfortunate that his ideas about where Polynesians originated from have been completely discredited.
transcript.zh: 他关于波利尼西亚人的起源的观点被证实完全是假的，实在是太遗憾了。

transcript.en: Yes.
transcript.zh: 是的。

transcript.en: Right, well, I'll prepare a PowerPoint slide at the end that acknowledges our sources.
transcript.zh: 是的，没错。对了，我在演讲结尾会准备一张幻灯片列出我们的资料来源。

transcript.en: I mainly used The Life and Work of Thor Heyerdahl by William Oliver.
transcript.zh: 我主要引用了William Oliver写的《The Life and Work of Thor Heyerdahl 》。

transcript.en: I thought the research methods he used were very sound, although I must say I found the overall tone somewhat old fashioned.
transcript.zh: 我觉得他使用的研究手法非常合理，不过有一点我不得不说的是，我发现这本书的总体语气有点过时。

transcript.en: I think they need to do a new, revised edition.
transcript.zh: 我觉得他们需要再发行一个新的修订版本。

transcript.en: Yeah, I agree.
transcript.zh: 是的，我同意。

transcript.en: What about the subject matter I found it really challenging!
transcript.zh: 主题怎么定呢？我觉得这个太有挑战性了。

transcript.en: Well, it's a complex issue .
transcript.zh: 这个问题挺复杂的......

transcript.en: I thought the book had lots of good points.
transcript.zh: 我觉得这本书里有很多不错的观点。
